neighbours.label: The connective that opens a justification after a prohibition or warning instruction (Never X, since ...; Do not X, because ...), vs the same connectives in descriptive past-tense statements
fire: Never prune roses in the frost, since the cut stems will die back badly.
Do not give the puppy grapes, because even a few can damage its kidneys.
Never leave a candle burning overnight, since a draft can tip the flame onto curtains.
Do not move the injured rider, since you may worsen a spinal injury.
Never mix bleach with ammonia, because the fumes are toxic.
Do not open the oven door early, since the cake will sink in the middle.
Never store the batteries in the car, because heat shortens their life.
Do not feed the ducks bread, since it fills them up without nourishing them.
quiet: We pruned the roses in late winter, since the weather had turned mild.
She gave the puppy a new collar, because the old one was worn.
He left the candle burning on the table, since the guests were still eating.
They moved the injured rider to the shade, because the sun was strong.
My father mixed the paint himself, because the store had closed.
We opened the oven door to check, since the timer had gone off.
I stored the batteries in a drawer, because the box was full.
The children fed the ducks seeds, since that was what the sign suggested.

predictions: 'since'/'because' right after a 'Never/Do not' instruction reaches 0.25-1.0; 'since'/'because' after a description of what someone did stays under 0.1.
notes: Card: peaks on '.', ' as', ' because', ' since', ';', ' -' after care/garden/medical instructions ('do not ... because'). Probe: 'Never cut the stems ..., since' 1.027, 'Do not water ..., because' 0.253, '.' after 'Do not try to straighten' 0.276; descriptive 'because we were home' 0.072, 'since it was late autumn' 0.027; 'as otherwise' 0.043 (weak).
